title: ～な — “don't ～!” (negative command)
summary: Attaching な to the dictionary form of a verb gives a blunt negative command: “don't ～!” It is used by men or in strong, direct situations such as warnings or signs, not in polite speech.

patterns.gloss: 触る → 触るな / 吸う → 吸うな / 話す → 話すな

body.p: It is the sentence-final particle な attached directly to the dictionary form: する becomes するな and 来る becomes 来るな. A reason is often added, as in 危ないから、触るな.
Use it for short, forceful orders: warning of danger, a parent scolding a child, signs and slogans (立ち入るな). Examples are ここでたばこを吸うな and 授業中に話すな.
It is a strong prohibition, so never use it to superiors or strangers. Politely, use ～ないでください or ～てはいけません; for a gentler casual tone, use ～ちゃだめ.

examples.ja: 危（あぶ）ないから、触（さわ）るな。
examples.tr: It's dangerous, so don't touch it.

examples.ja: ここでたばこを吸（す）うな。
examples.romaji: Koko de tabako o suu na.

examples.ja: 授業中（じゅぎょうちゅう）に話（はな）すな。

pitfalls: This final な is a strong order; do not use it with superiors or people you have just met.
Attach it to the dictionary form (食べるな), not the ない form (食べないな).
